\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{রোবট} (robôṭ)}{রোবট (robôṭ)}]{\bn{রোবট} (robôṭ) — a robot}

\label{lesson:BN-C504-robot}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a screen, then the Bengali for to download.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{রোবট}}
\textbf{\bn{রোবট}} — \emph{robôṭ} — \textquotedblleft{}a robot\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{এই} \bn{কারখানায়} \bn{রোবটরা} \bn{গাড়ি} \bn{বানায়।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Ei kārkhānāy robôṭrā gāṛi bānāy.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In this factory robots build cars.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{রোবট}} (\emph{robôṭ}) is borrowed from English \emph{robot}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{robôṭ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{robôṭ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Ei kārkhānāy robôṭrā gāṛi bānāy.} — In this factory robots build cars.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a screen, then the Bengali for to download, then say \emph{robôṭ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{রোবট} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A robot\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{স্বয়ংক্রিয়} (svôyôngkriyô)}{স্বয়ংক্রিয় (svôyôngkriyô)}]{\bn{স্বয়ংক্রিয়} (svôyôngkriyô) — automatic}

\label{lesson:BN-C504-svoyongkriyo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to download, then the Bengali for a robot.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{স্বয়ংক্রিয়}}
\textbf{\bn{স্বয়ংক্রিয়}} — \emph{svôyôngkriyô} — \textquotedblleft{}automatic\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sṭeshôner dôrjāṭā svôyôngkriyô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The station's door is automatic.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{স্বয়ংক্রিয়}} (\emph{svôyôngkriyô}) joins Sanskrit \emph{svayam}, \textquotedblleft{}by oneself\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{kriyā}, \textquotedblleft{}doing, action\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams): working by itself.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{জং} \bn{ধরা} (jông dhôrā)}{জং ধরা (jông dhôrā)}]{\bn{জং} \bn{ধরা} (jông dhôrā) — to rust}

\label{lesson:BN-C504-jong-dhora}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for automatic, then the Bengali for a generator.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{জং} \bn{ধরা}}
\textbf{\bn{জং} \bn{ধরা}} — \emph{jông dhôrā} — \textquotedblleft{}to rust\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{বৃষ্টিতে} \bn{পেরেকগুলোতে} \bn{জং} \bn{ধরল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Brishṭite perekgulote jông dhôrlô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The nails rusted in the rain.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{সাইকেলে} \bn{জং} \bn{ধরল}, \emph{sei sāikele jông dhôrlô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{জং} \bn{ধরা}} (\emph{jông dhôrā}) joins \bn{জং}, \textquotedblleft{}rust\textquotedblright{}, usually traced to Persian \emph{zang}, to \bn{ধরা}, \textquotedblleft{}to catch, to take hold\textquotedblright{}: rust takes hold.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{Brishṭite perekgulote jông dhôrlô.} — The nails rusted in the rain.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for automatic, then the Bengali for a generator, then say \emph{jông dhôrā} again
\end{itemize}
